themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: The election hit the suppliers of the AI build, not the buyers. On Nov 4 CoreWeave fell 9.90%, Nebius 6.67%, Nvidia 3.17% and Lumentum 7.85%, while Microsoft rose 6.68% and Amazon 6.12% (Massive). After the close Qualcomm guided below estimates and fell about 9% premarket, while Coherent beat with data center and communications revenue up 79% to $1.95 billion and guided above estimates (CNBC, MoneyCheck). Korea's KOSPI fell 5.28% on Nov 5 with SK hynix down 9.46% (Korea Exchange via FN News).
themes.for_you: Long term: MSFT ran 5% above the top of its buy zone, so it is no longer a buy now name. No puts on chip or neocloud names while the group falls. SMH fell 2.75% on Nov 4 and was down more than 3% premarket Nov 5.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: The AI power trade sold off hard on Nov 4 after Democrats won Congress and Texas elected a governor who campaigned on a pause for new data centers. Vistra fell 13.83%, Vertiv 12.89%, Eaton 9.86%, GE Vernova 9.30% and Constellation 6.71% (Massive). Goldman estimates state moratoriums could put about 45% of planned US data center capacity at risk; Wells Fargo says Texas holds about 27% of it (Yahoo, CNBC).
themes.for_you: No new swings or puts in power names until the selling stops; heavy volume down days are distribution. Vistra reports Nov 6, a second event risk. Watch whether Vertiv's order backlog holds up in the next quarter; the fear is about permits, not current demand.

themes.name: Critical materials and geopolitics
themes.what: China's one year pause of its October 2025 rare earth export rules ends Nov 10, and no extension notice was found as of Nov 4 to 5 (Mining.com, Motley Fool). MP Materials fell 5.08% to 35.91 on Nov 4 (Massive), near a 16 month low, and reports Q3 after today's close.
themes.for_you: No action before Nov 10. If China lets the pause lapse, US magnet makers get a policy tailwind but buyers face shortages; MP also reports tonight, so no swing or put in MP this week.

themes.name: Defense, drones and reshoring
themes.what: Defense stocks fell on Nov 4 on fears a Democratic Congress trims the Pentagon budget: Lockheed fell 6.88%, L3Harris 6.46%, Northrop 4.53% and RTX 2.64% (Massive). Jefferies expects the 2027 budget nearer the House's roughly $1.15 trillion than the $1.5 trillion request, and TD Cowen called Golden Dome and Golden Fleet most at risk and nuclear modernization least at risk (Reuters via US News).
themes.for_you: LHX, RTX and GD stay 'Accumulate on pullback' and all three are still above their zones (Nov 4: LHX 259.74, RTX 198.43, GD 364.87). No puts on defense into budget fights.

themes.name: Fintech and Crypto Rails: Stablecoins, Tokenization, Exchanges
themes.what: Remitly reported Q3 on Nov 4: revenue $509.8 million, up 22%; send volume $24.4 billion, up 25%; 10.3 million active customers; net income $67.6 million; and a full year revenue outlook of $1.989 to $1.991 billion. The buyback authorization rose from $200 million to $500 million (SEC 8-K, TipRanks). Affirm reports after today's close, with a 2pm Pacific call.
themes.for_you: RELY (27.08 Nov 4) is not on a buy list; the after hours move was not found. AFRM reports tonight: no new put or buy until the first close after the report.

themes.name: GLP-1 and obesity
themes.what: Novo Nordisk's Q3 beat on its Wegovy pill: pill sales were DKK 5.39 billion against DKK 4.62 billion expected, and it raised 2026 sales guidance to minus 2% to plus 2% at constant currency. Injectable Wegovy fell 13%, and US list prices for Wegovy and Ozempic drop to $675 a month from Jan 1, 2027 (CNBC, Nov 4). NVO closed up 4.95% at 42.18 (Massive).
themes.for_you: No action. The pill is pulling patients from the injection, so price, not demand, is the risk. LLY stays 'Accumulate on pullback', far above its zone at 1,417.99.

themes.name: Healthcare and Medtech: Aging, Heart, Sugar, Hearing, Sight
themes.what: Medtech, hospitals and Medicaid insurers rallied on Nov 4 on bets a Democratic Congress delays Medicaid cuts: Intuitive Surgical rose 9.38%, Stryker 9.37%, HCA 10.34%, Medtronic 6.15%, Dexcom 6.64% and Insulet 6.56% (Massive; Investrade). Zoetis reported Q3 this morning: revenue $2.39 billion, down 1%, adjusted EPS $1.75 against $1.51 expected by Zacks, and it raised full year adjusted EPS guidance to $6.25 to $6.35 (AP).
themes.for_you: No chasing. MDT (104.96) and PODD (165.02) are 'Accumulate on pullback' and MDT is well above its 84.35 to 94.36 zone. A one day policy pop often fades; wait for the dashboard's refresh before any medtech swing.

themes.name: Space, Quantum and Cyber: Government Funded Frontier Tech
themes.what: ARK bought SpaceX (SPCX) in three funds on Nov 4 (about 348,000 shares across ARKK, ARKQ and ARKW, ARK email) while the stock fell 3.81% to 135.92 with the AI and Musk names (Massive, CNBC).
themes.for_you: No action. SPCX is on the Lineup but has no buy verdict or setup; one fund buying is a weak signal. Left out of both lists: ARK bought while the price fell.

innovations.name: Healthcare
innovations.what: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill sold DKK 5.39 billion in Q3, above the DKK 4.62 billion forecast, and lifted combined US Wegovy sales 21% even as the injection fell 13%. Novo raised its 2026 sales guide and cuts US list prices for Wegovy and Ozempic to $675 a month from Jan 1, 2027 (CNBC, Nov 4).
innovations.for_you: No action. Oral GLP-1s are taking share from shots; lower prices from January are the risk. NVO closed at 42.18 on Nov 4, up 4.95% (Massive).

innovations.name: Materials
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Navitas Q3 2026 revenue was $14.0 million, up 38% from a year earlier and above guidance, with high power revenue up more than 50% from Q2; it guides Q4 to $16.0 million (SEC filings). Still tiny, so the stage stays early adoption.
innovations.for_you: No action. NVTS is not on a buy list and still loses about $34 million a quarter from operations.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.what: Copom held the Selic at 13.75% on Nov 4, unanimously, and ended the cuts that began in March. 72 of 105 institutions expected the hold and 33 a cut to 13.50%, so part of the market was surprised. The statement cited the dollar, El Nino and inflation expectations above target and gave no guidance for December (Poder360, Sou Brasilia, Revista Oeste).
countries.for_you: No Brazil buys or puts. High rates for longer weigh on lenders like NU, ITUB and BBD. EWZ closed at 32.25 on Nov 4, before the decision (Massive); watch its first reaction today.

countries.name: China
countries.what: Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose about 3.67% on Nov 5 and the Hang Seng Tech index about 5.55%, its best day since February 2025, as money rotated out of AI hardware into cheaper Chinese internet names; Alibaba rose more than 8% and Tencent more than 7% (Bloomberg, BigGo Finance). Southbound funds were net sellers of more than HK$21.3 billion. FXI rose 4.22% to 34.59 on Nov 4 (Massive).
countries.for_you: No action. One rotation day is not a trend, and mainland buyers were selling. No China puts.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4.00% from 3.75% on Nov 5 in an 8 to 1 vote, its first hike in more than three years; Catherine Mann voted for 4.25%. The Bank tied the move to Middle East energy costs feeding into other prices. Next decision Dec 17 (Bank of England, FXStreet).
countries.for_you: No action. A hike while oil is falling shows central banks still fear inflation; that keeps pressure on long rates everywhere. EWU closed at 48.93 on Nov 4, before the decision (Massive).

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: Brent fell 9.73% to settle at $93.52 on Nov 4, the lowest since Aug 31, on bets of a US and Iran deal (FinanceFeeds). One report says the US approved a Qatar draft memorandum; Iran called the US reply 'not convincing' and says Hormuz stays shut until its conditions are met (HNGN, Korea Herald). USO fell 8.07% and XLE 4.74% (Massive).
countries.for_you: Swing: all four oil plans (XOM, CVX, COP, EOG) hit their stops on Nov 4. No new energy swings or puts until oil finds a floor; the deal is not signed and Hormuz is still shut.

countries.name: Japan
countries.what: Toyota's Tokyo shares rose about 16.7% on Nov 5 after July to September operating profit rose 34% to about 1.13 trillion yen and it raised its full year operating profit forecast to 3.9 trillion yen from 3.4 trillion, helped by a weak yen and hybrids. China sales fell 12%. The Nikkei fell about 2.15%, led by chip names like Advantest (TipRanks, Investing.com).
countries.for_you: No action. TM ADR closed at 199.46 on Nov 4, before the report (Massive). A big gap after a report is not an entry; wait for a base.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The KOSPI fell 5.28% to 5,383.80 on Nov 5 as the US election raised fears of limits on AI data centers. Samsung Electronics fell 7.57% and SK hynix 9.46%, and foreign investors sold about 2.7 trillion won of the two (Korea Exchange via FN News, Korea Times).
countries.for_you: No Korea or memory trades. EWY fell 1.90% to 152.12 on Nov 4 (Massive) and will open lower today. Wait for a calm week.
